import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Fill NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' with 'No Disorder' for clearer categorization
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Set a visually appealing style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a figure with two subplots to compare Sleep Duration and Quality across disorders
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 6)) # Adjust figure size for better readability

# Plot 1: Box plot for Sleep Duration by Sleep Disorder
sns.boxplot(x='Sleep Disorder', y='Sleep Duration', data=df, ax=axes[0])
axes[0].set_title('Sleep Duration by Sleep Disorder', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Sleep Disorder', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=15) # Rotate labels slightly if they overlap

# Plot 2: Box plot for Quality of Sleep by Sleep Disorder
sns.boxplot(x='Sleep Disorder', y='Quality of Sleep', data=df, ax=axes[1])
axes[1].set_title('Quality of Sleep by Sleep Disorder', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Sleep Disorder', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=15) # Rotate labels slightly if they overlap

# Add a main title for the entire figure to provide context
fig.suptitle('Impact of Sleep Disorders on Sleep Duration and Quality', fontsize=16, y=1.02)

# Adjust layout to prevent titles and labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.98]) # Adjust rect to make space for suptitle

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
